item.title: From Shock to Strength: The Endogenous Foundations of Entrepreneurship under Adversity
item.content:encoded:
Dafna Kariv, Reichman University

Mark Sanders, Maastricht University

Trent Williams, Brigham Young University

Friederike Welter, University of Siegen

David Audretsch, Indiana University

This special issue examines how entrepreneurs develop internal resources and psychological strengths that enable them to succeed when external support systems are unavailable or depleted. The collection challenges the traditional view of crises as isolated events, recognizing instead that modern entrepreneurs frequently operate under continuous adversity and must rely on their own innovation, adaptability, and resilience to thrive.

The special issue invites research exploring the endogenous foundations of entrepreneurial success—the internal capabilities, mechanisms, and strengths that allow entrepreneurs to survive and flourish despite lacking adequate ecosystem support. The collection seeks bold, groundbreaking research that fundamentally advances understanding of how entrepreneurs draw upon internal resources to achieve success under sustained challenging conditions.

Appel publié par Small Business Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Endogenous capabilities and internal resources in entrepreneurship
  • Psychological strengths and resilience
  • Entrepreneurial success amid adversity
  • Innovation and adaptability under stress
  • Self-generated mechanisms for survival
  • Entrepreneurship without ecosystem support

item.title: Entrepreneurship and the Creation of Decent Work for All
item.content:encoded:
This multi-journal collection addresses the relationship between entrepreneurship and the creation of decent work, aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 8. The collection recognizes that societal changes, environmental crises, and economic disruptions significantly impact employment quality and labor market conditions, and that entrepreneurship may serve as a critical mechanism for generating productive employment and fair working conditions.

The collection seeks to gather diverse scholarly perspectives on how entrepreneurship can contribute to achieving full and productive employment with decent wages, improved labor market access, and better job opportunities. Submissions may be research or review articles and will undergo rigorous peer review according to each participating journal's standards, with accepted articles published in the submitting journal and highlighted in the collection.

Appel publié par Small Business Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Equal pay for work of equal value
  • Gender discrimination in employment
  • Immigration and employment

  • Modern slavery and child labor
  • Labor policy
  • Entrepreneurial enterprises, SMEs, and family businesses
  • Global entrepreneurial firms
  • Remote work
  • Opportunity entrepreneurship
  • Measuring externalities of new businesses

item.title: Entrepreneurship, Creative Destruction, and Growth: Enriching the Aghion-Howitt Tradition
item.content:encoded:
Philippe Aghion, Collège de France

Martin Andersson, Blekinge Institute of Technology

David B. Audretsch, Indiana University

Maksim Belitski, University of Reading

Pontus Braunerhjelm, KTH Royal Institute of Technology

This special issue seeks to advance research connecting entrepreneurial activity across multiple analytical levels, from individual firm behavior to regional systems and national policy environments. The editors invite studies examining the full lifecycle of ventures—from formation through scaling, exit, and the broader dynamics through which innovation translates into economic growth—grounded in Schumpeterian economics and the Aghion-Howitt tradition.

Submissions may also explore how entrepreneurship research perspectives can extend and enrich the Aghion-Howitt framework, bridging theoretical and empirical insights from both literatures.

Appel publié par Small Business Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Entrepreneurship research frameworks
